 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2541 of 2013
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the impugned order dated 15.03.2013 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- IX Additional District Judge, Chittoor, passed in M.V.O.P.No.204 of 2006, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim against the respondents 3 and 4, the instant appeal is preferred by the appellant-Respondent No.4- Insurance Company.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- IX Additional District Judge, Chittoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under sections 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 28.08.2004.

4. The facts germane to dispose of this appeal may be briefly stated as follows:
2 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 On 28.08.2004 at about 3.00 p.m. while the petitioner was travelling in the Tempo bearing No.TN 37 D 1847 in the capacity of owner of goods from Panapakam to Palamaner, when the tempo vehicle was proceeding on Bangalore-Palamaner National High Way, MBT road and when it reached near M.V.Giri, Bangarupalem Mandal, Chittoor District, the driver of Tempo vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car bearing No.KA 01Z 2624, which is coming in opposite direction in a negligent manner, resulting which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
5. The first and third respondents remained exparte.

The second respondent filed counter and pleaded that the driver of the car bearing No.KA 01Z 2624 has not been charged by the Station House Officer, Bangarupalem and the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the Tempo bearing No.TN37D 1847.
The fourth respondent filed counter and pleaded that the driver of the car bearing No.KA 01Z 2624,
which belongs to first respondent, came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed 3 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 against the Tempo bearing No.TN 37D 1847 and the Tempo vehicle does not have goods carrier permit to ply in Andhra Pradesh.
6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
Unknown vs Judgment on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20548263/
1 i.

Whether the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 1st respondent's car bearing No.KA 01Z 2624 or due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 3 rd respondent's Tempo bearing No.TN 37D 1847 or both?
ii. Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?
iii. To what relief?
7. During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A10 and Ex.X1 to Ex.X3 were marked.
On behalf of respondents RW1 was examined and on behalf of 4th respondent Ex.B1 was marked, on behalf of 2nd respondent Ex.B1 to Ex.B3 were marked.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal 4 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tempo/mini lorry and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.1,74,630/- to the claimant towards compensation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the fourth respondent Insurance Company filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.

9. Heard the learned counsel for appellant-respondent No.4 and the learned counsel for claimant and respondents 1 to 3.
10.

Now, the point for consideration is:
 Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any  interference?
If so, to what extent?

11. POINT :-
The case of the claimant is that the drivers of the car and Tempo bearing Nos.KA 01Z 2624 and TN 37D 1847 belongs to respondents 1 and 3 respectively drove the vehicles in a rash and negligent manner on 28.08.2004 at about 3.00 p.m. and dashed against each other while coming in opposite direction, as a result of which, these two vehicles were damaged, the Tempo vehicle turned turtle on the left side of the road and the petitioner, who was 5 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 travelling in the Tempo in the capacity of the owner of the goods from Panapakam to Palamaner, sustained multiple bleeding and fracture injuries and he was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor, later he was shifted to C.M.C. Hospital, Vellore, where he underwent treatment and spent more than Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses.
12.
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., Tempo vehicle, the petitioner relied on his sole testimony as PW1.

In his evidence, he reiterated the contents of the petition that both the drivers of the car and Tempo respectively drove the vehicles in a rash and negligent manner without due care and caution and dashed against each other.

He Unknown vs Judgment on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20548263/
2
further admits that a case in Crime No.408 of 2004 under Section 337 and 304-A of Indian Penal Code 1860 has been registered against the driver of the Tempo vehicle.

Ex.A3 certified copy of charge sheet goes to show that after completion of investigation, the Station House Officer,
Bangarupalem Police Station filed a charge sheet against the driver of the Tempo vehicle in the Court of IV Additional Munsif Magistrate, Chittoor.
6 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 13.
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the petitioner relied on the evidence of PW2, who is none other than the driver of the Tempo.

As per the evidence of PW2,
the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car, but not due to his negligence.
He is a driver of the offending vehicle, naturally he will deny his rash and negligent driving.

Therefore, it is not safe to rely on the evidence of PW2.
14.
The petitioner filed a petition for claiming compensation in respect of injury sustained in a Motor Vehicle accident.
The initial burden is on the petitioner to show that there was a rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident.
As stated supra, PW2 is none other than the driver of the offending vehicle, therefore, it is not safe to rely on the evidence of PW2.

The material on record reveals that Ex.A1 First Information Report is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., PW2 and after completion of investigation, the Station House Officer laid charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., Tempo vehicle.
The documentary evidence filed by the petitioner, i.e., Ex.A1 and Ex.A3, clearly goes to show that the driver of the Tempo 7 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 drove the Tempo in a rash and negligent manner.

On appreciation of the entire evidence on record, by giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo/mini lorry.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
15. Coming to the compensation, in order to prove the injuries, the petitioner relied on the evidence of PW3.
PW3 is the doctor, who treated PW1.
As per his evidence coupled with the documentary evidence Ex.A2 certified copy of wound certificate, the petitioner sustained one simple injury and four grievous injuries.
The Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- each for four grievous injuries and Rs.2,500/- for one simple injury i.e., an amount of Rs.42,500/- was awarded under the head of pain and suffering.
The Tribunal, on considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, an amount of Rs.10,000/- was awarded under the head of loss of amenities of life.

The Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- under the head of discomfort and inconvenience, since the petitioner sustained one simple injury and four grievous injuries in the accident 8 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 for no fault of him.

The Tribunal, on considering Ex.A6 bunch of medical bills,
awarded an amount of Rs.16,738/- towards medical expenses.
The Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.2,000/- towards attendant charges and an amount of Rs.5,000/- for special diet and feeding charges and an amount of Rs.2,000/- towards transport expenses.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the above finding given by the Tribunal in awarding the compensation under the above heads.
Unknown vs Judgment on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20548263/

3 16. The Tribunal on considering the evidence of PW1 and also on considering the evidence of PW4,
who issued Ex.A9 disability certificate, came to conclusion that the petitioner is suffering with disability of 20% and his annual income is arrived at Rs.36,000/- and awarded an amount of Rs.86,400/- towards loss of future earnings under the head of permanent disability.

In fact, the income of the petitioner per annum is Rs.36,000/- and disability sustained by the petitioner is 20%
and multiplier applicable to the age group of the petitioner is 18, the petitioner is entitled an amount of Rs.1,29,600/- towards loss of future earnings under the head of permanent disability, however the Tribunal awarded an amount of 9 VGKRJ MACMA 2541 of 2013 Rs.86,400/- under the said head.
The claimant did not file any cross objections against the said finding given by the Tribunal.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal in awarding Rs.86,400/- under the head of loss of future earnings under permanent disability.
By giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.1,74,630/- towards total compensation.

17. For the foregoing reasons, I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in awarding compensation of Rs.1,74,630/- with interest at 7.5% p.a. to the petitioner against the respondents 3 and 4 and the award passed by the Tribunal is perfectly sustainable under law and it requires no interference.
18. Resultantly, this appeal is dismissed, confirming the award passed by the Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO, J Dated: 14.08.2023.
